claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside it inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends structuring Git repositories for publishing packages per the strategies described in this guide (one package per repository, cohesive components).
For a source-based plugin package, the package's version is the Git tag on the repository.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository.

Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow (apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish`), typically performed by a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
Publishing a source-based package to the Private Registry requires applying a semver Git tag (e.g., `v1.2.3`) to the repository.
`pulumi package publish` sends the package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
The `pulumi package publish` step in a CI/CD pipeline often runs automated tests before publishing.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry.
Source-based packages referenced directly from a `Pulumi.yaml` file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
For an executable-based package, the package's version is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
Executable-based package releases are produced by a CI/CD pipeline that builds the plugin, generates the SDKs, and pushes everything to the relevant feeds.
In both source-based and executable-based cases, the released artifact is a single, semantically-versioned Pulumi package.
A repository should contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type; this is Pulumi's recommended approach.
A repository containing multiple Pulumi packages must either release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that fights the way Pulumi naturally consumes packages.
Multiple components inside a single Pulumi package are fine and expected, and the components ship together at the package's version.
Pulumi recommends defining exactly one package per repository, grouping a cohesive set of components inside that package, and using multiple repositories (one per package) for distinct packages.

The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry (https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/eks/) bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with the supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
The components in the Amazon EKS package are almost always used together and tend to evolve together.
A single `PulumiPlugin.yaml` at the repository root defines a package, with its components living alongside it.
The example repository layout for a package has PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repo root and components in a `components/` directory (EksCluster/, EksIam/).

Using a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components is technically possible but Pulumi does not recommend it because it forfeits meaningful semantic versioning.
When unrelated components share a package, every release of the package versions every component the same way, regardless of whether each component changed, which violates semver.

In a package containing two unrelated components, an enhancement to ComponentA releases the package at v1.1.0 and a breaking change to ComponentB releases it at v2.0.0, versioning both components with the package version.
Pulumi's documentation on publishing packages exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/publishing-packages/.
Pulumi docs pages exist at /docs/iac/concepts/packages/ and /docs/iac/concepts/components/.

Pulumi docs pages exist at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/packaging-components/ with sections 'source-based-plugin-packages' and 'executable-based-plugin-packages', /docs/idp/concepts/private-registry/, and /docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_package_publish/.
